transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-11 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dana (Head of ML, Northreach), Priya (Platform Eng), Ethan (CTO)

Summary: Quick QBR-style health check focused on operational economics (latency v cost), runway for production rollout, and alignment on pilot scope. Customer shared recent adoption spike and a couple of infra constraints (VPC egress limits, KMS key rotation cadence). Redwood suggested a small-batch pilot + KV-cache tuning and provided initial pricing tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated.

Topics: usage trends, cost spikes, latency p95/p99, private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS), pilot scope and success criteria, next steps for benchmarks and security docs.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Liam will run the infra bits. Dana, Priya, Ethan, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Dana: Hey Maya, thanks. Sorry ran a little late, we were in a backlog sync.
[00:22] Priya: all good.
[00:25] Liam: no worries, shall we jump into the metrics you sent over, Dana? The spike monday looked like a 2.7x burst.
[00:35] Dana: yeah Monday was weird — we had a campaign push, ended up with higher concurrent chat sessions. Our average tokens per request stayed same but concurrency blew up so p95 moved from 220ms to 800ms on our current single-zone setup.
[00:48] Ethan: and cost bumped too, we saw a 40% spend increase for that day, which flagged finance.
[00:55] Maya: right, that's what we wanted to root cause with you today — where latency vs cost tradeoffs are acceptable and whether dedicated or hosted makes sense long term.
[01:07] Priya: quick note — we have restrictive egress in our VPC and a strict KMS rotation policy, which affects long-lived connections for on-prem style deployments.
[01:20] Liam: ok, that helps explain why your connection churn might be high. For the burst, two immediate levers are batching and KV cache warmup; we can also recommend a small dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
[01:34] Dana: when you say KV cache warmup — we've had some docs but our cache misses are still high, could be due to prompt variability.
[01:42] Liam: yes prompt variance kills prefix cache efficiency. We can profile the top 100 prompts and suggest prefix normalization or a micro-cache that pins tokens for those.
[01:52] Priya: is that something you can do in hosted mode? We prefer not to run private yet because of the SSO constraints with our legacy IdP.
[02:02] Maya: absolutely — hosted supports workload-aware caching and can set tenant-level cache policies. The tradeoff is cost transparency and some data residency controls are limited unless you go private.
[02:14] Ethan: hmm, residency is a later ask, right now it's mostly audit logs and KMS integration that matter. We need HSM/KMS server side encryption for certain datasets.
[02:24] Liam: we support KMS integrations for Private and for Dedicated via customer-managed keys; hosted can integrate with a proxy KMS for some customers, but for full HSM you'd want Private.
[02:35] Dana: sounds like Private could be the long-term path. For now, though, what's the quick win to reduce p95 without increasing monthly burn?
[02:45] Liam: two paths: tuning batch sizes to reduce per-token cost or adding a small reserved pool to absorb peaks. For short term, smart batching + auto-eviction cache tuning usually drops p95 by ~30% and lowers per-token cost via better GPU utilization — but it adds a bit of tail latency for single-request cases.
[03:05] Maya: and to quantify — for your traffic mix, we estimated in the deck a 15-25% cost reduction with configured batching; switching to a 1-2 GPU dedicated pool would add a fixed monthly commit but could cut burst p99s significantly.
[03:22] Priya: can you walk through the math again? finance will want breakout of fixed vs variable.
[03:28] Maya: sure, we can share a pricing worksheet. Quick sketch: hosted pay-as-you-go tokens + model costs vs dedicated where you commit to X capacity. Example — at your 50k QPS/day baseline, dedicated reduces per-token unit cost by ~18% if utilization stays above 60%. We will send the spreadsheet with a scenario table.
[03:48] Dana: fine, please send. Also curious about quantization or smaller model variants for lower latency.
[03:55] Liam: model variant routing is a thing — smart routing can fall back to a quantized or smaller model for non-critical queries. That helps with cost but can impact output quality. We usually recommend a split test with evals.
[04:10] Ethan: what about the evals — will Redwood run those or we do in-house? We have a small eval harness but no large holdout set.
[04:18] Maya: we can run initial evals against your prompts as part of the pilot. We'll define metric thresholds (F1 for extraction tasks, BLEU-ish score if you have generation-quality metrics).
[04:30] Priya: security docs — can you send SOC2, ISO, and the KMS integration guide? Our audit team will want them.
[04:38] Liam: yes, I'll drop the SOC2 report, iso cert summary, and a short note on SAML/SCIM integration. For KMS specifics, there's a one-page how-to for Private deployments.
[04:50] Dana: excellent. A sequencing question — pilot first then private? or pilot as dedicated?
[04:58] Maya: I'd recommend pilot in hosted with tuned batching + cache to prove the workload and collect traces; if the security bar prevents you from using hosted for the pilot, we can spin up a short-term dedicated snapshot in your VPC. Both have tradeoffs for speed and auditability.
[05:16] Ethan: latency SLOs — we need p95 under 350ms for conversational UI, and p99 under 900ms. Can you meet that in hosted?
[05:24] Liam: with caching and batching we are optimistic. We'll need your traffic trace though. If your workload has many single-turn queries, tail can be tough. The pilot will validate.
[05:34] Dana: ok we can share the trace. Also, about autoscale — our concern is cold start ramp and scheduler time.
[05:41] Liam: Redwood's autoscaler has burst capacity and can pre-warm based on traffic predictions. For Private/Dedicated we can configure buffer capacity and warm pools to reduce cold starts.
[05:51] Priya: any constraints on VPC egress or specific ports? we lock down egress generally.
[05:57] Liam: for Private you can keep traffic internal; for hosted you need outbound TLS to Redwood endpoints. We'll document the minimal egress rules.
[06:06] Maya: let's surface the immediate timeline — Northreach wants to go to a small external beta in November?
[06:12] Ethan: yes, November external beta. Internal rollout earlier November 1 if possible.
[06:18] Maya: so pilot must start mid-October to give ops time. That fits with the dates we proposed.
[06:24] Dana: yes. "mid-October" is our target.
[06:28] Liam: on the pilot scope — we'll run a 48-72 hour baseline with two configs: 1) hosted tuned batching+cache, 2) small dedicated snapshot (if you allow). We'll collect p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1k-tokens.
[06:44] Priya: please also collect trace annotated with request types so we can map heavy queries to endpoints.
[06:50] Liam: yep, we'll include request-type tagging.
[06:53] Maya: ok quick check on risks — any regulatory or data residency blockers?
[06:58] Ethan: not yet, but our legal team will ask if user data leaves the region.
[07:03] Maya: noted. We'll include region mapping and data flow in the security packet.
[07:08] Dana: a small thing — during the last spike our retry logic doubled upstream requests which worsened the burst. We fixed the client but want to avoid similar in future. Can Redwood help with circuit-breaker recommendations?
[07:20] Liam: we have recommended client-side patterns (exponential backoff, jitter) and server-side rate limiting. We'll share a snippet and a sample middleware for node/python.
[07:30] Priya: that would be super helpful.
[07:32] Maya: ok, we're nearing time so let's recap next steps.
[07:35] Dana: go ahead.
[07:36] Maya: Next steps: you (Dana) share traffic trace + top prompts by 10/15, Redwood runs 48h pilot starting 10/18 (hosted tuned config) and share p95/p99 and cost metrics by 10/22. Liam will send SOC2/ISO/KMS notes by 10/14. Maya will send pricing sheet same day.
[07:56] Ethan: sounds good.
[08:00] Priya: quick question — about model rollouts, can you do canary traffic split on model variants?
[08:06] Liam: yes, we support canary and A/B routing with auto-fallback. We'll show how to configure traffic split in the console.
[08:14] Maya: perfect. Any final questions?
[08:18] Dana: none from me. thanks.
[08:20] Ethan: all good. thanks team.
[08:23] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms: "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "quants" for quantization in the rough auto transcript. Small crosstalk at 00:22.
